_meta.description: Static AI-written scouting reports, one per owner — the back of each trading card. Generated once from league data and not recomputed by the app.

summaries.jmuggy20: The winningest owner in league history. 140 career wins, a record thirteen playoff trips, and three titles (2009, 2017, 2021) spread across three different eras — nobody has been good for longer. Seven trips to the final is the stuff of legend; losing four of them is the stuff of therapy. And somewhere, b50rock still brings up the 147-point beating from 2014.
summaries.RichoSuave: The dynasty. Four championships — 2011, 2014, 2023, 2025 — the most banners in the rafters, including back-to-back-adjacent titles to close out the modern era. Eleven playoff runs and a seven-game heater in 2023. Just don't ask about the 2025 crown: a 7–7 regular season remains the most mediocre path to a ring ever recorded. Royalty, but royalty that snuck in through the service entrance.
summaries.jstoll65: Two-time champion (2013, 2015) and the league's most reliable menace — 134 wins, eleven playoff berths, and personal ownership of half the league (10–1 over njohnson9352, 14–5 over juicebox269). Six finals appearances is elite; losing four of them earned him the crown he never wanted: king of the bridesmaids.
summaries.kevinconklin05: The 2012 champion and author of the league's most untouchable record: ten straight wins in 2010. Twelve playoff appearances and 131 career victories put him firmly among the founding-father elite. Since the title, though, it's been three runner-up finishes and a growing collection of silver medals — always the artist, rarely the closer. The 140-point flattening by juicebox269 in 2015 is not to be mentioned at the draft.
summaries.Dieselbaron: Two banners, eight years apart (2010, 2018) — proof he can win in any decade he feels like showing up for. Seventeen seasons of trench warfare with jmuggy20 in the league's longest-running rivalry. The catch: an almost perfectly even 114–112 career record, a 3–11 faceplant in 2022, and a 1–6 record against frolickingjester, a man who joined the league twelve years after he did.
summaries.adrenth01: Champion in 2016 and 2020, with a six-game streak in 2013 and the joint-biggest blowout in league history (+136 over CheezeBallHustle, whom he beat 9 times in 10 meetings — a legal form of bullying). Seventeen seasons, eight playoff runs, forever dangerous. Forever, that is, except against jstoll65, who has beaten him 22 times and counting.
summaries.b50rock: The 2019 champion and owner of the single most violent result in league history: a +147 annihilation of jmuggy20 in 2014 that's still spoken of in hushed tones. Ten playoff berths, a 2,103-point season in 2021, and a five-game streak all the way back in 2011. One banner from ten October runs is the resume of a man who peaks exactly one week too early.
summaries.juicebox269: The 2022 champion, and he did it in style — 2,135 points that season, one of the great offensive campaigns ever assembled. Nine playoff trips over sixteen seasons and a habit of delivering historic beatdowns (ask kevinconklin05 about 2015). But the ledger shows a career 5–14 record against jstoll65, and a quiet exit after 2024 — the throne was rented, never owned.
summaries.MattMattMatt85: Instant history: a championship in 2024, just his third season, behind 2,099 points of pure fireworks. The sequel was less cinematic — a 2–12 title defense in 2025 that stands as the fastest fall from grace the league has ever witnessed. Champion to cellar in twelve months; even the trophy looked surprised.
summaries.espn13495523: One season, one finals run. Arrived in 2025, rattled off a six-game win streak, and marched a 7–7 roster all the way to the championship game before RichoSuave ended the fairy tale. A debut that promising deserves a banner someday — and maybe, eventually, an actual display name.
summaries.espn75676325: The best owner without a ring, full stop. A .604 career win rate and six playoff berths in seven seasons — nobody active is more consistent. He's a perfect 6–0 against Rodney19140 and terrorizes the middle class. But 2–7 against kevinconklin05 and zero banners means the resume reads: great regular seasons, allergic to jewelry.
summaries.frolickingjester: The league's premier giant-slayer: 6–1 lifetime against two-time champ Dieselbaron and with a winning record against most of the old guard. A dead-even 35–35 career and a 2024 breakout (1,973 points) suggest the best is coming. The 1–7 mark against jmuggy20, however, suggests the best will have to go through someone who owns him completely.
summaries.joe52690: Fifteen consecutive seasons of showing up — the league's iron man — crowned by a 2019 run to the final and a 2,014-point outburst in 2022. Loyalty like that builds leagues. It also builds records: most career losses in history (122), a 1–12 campaign in 2014, and a 2–9 lifetime mark against frolickingjester. The heart of the league, if not its trophy case.
summaries.CheezeBallHustle: Nine seasons of grind with three playoff appearances and a genuine heater in 2014 (four straight wins). Peaked at 4th — respectable! The exit was less so: a 2–11 farewell tour in 2020, and a career 1–9 record against adrenth01 that included a 136-point demolition. Some rivalries are competitive. That one was a subscription to pain.
summaries.Rodney19140: A decade of service with a genuine top-3 finish to his name and the occasional haymaker — a +115 knockout of eventual-champ adrenth01 in 2014 proved he could beat anyone on his day. His day came rarely: 43–88 overall, an 0–6 record against espn75676325, nine losses in eleven meetings with RichoSuave, and a 1–13 farewell in 2021. Beloved. Farmed.
summaries.njohnson9352: Came out firing with 1,869 points as a rookie in 2011 — a debut most owners never top — and hung around for eight seasons of honest football, peaking at 5th. Unfortunately, the league's aristocracy treated him as a renewable resource: 1–10 against jstoll65, 1–7 against b50rock, and the preferred victim of three different champions. A good man in a bad neighborhood.
summaries.Charlie Walls: One season, 2011, and one moment of glory: a 73-point statement win over future champion kevinconklin05. Went 5–8, finished 9th, and walked away forever. Some men touch the flame once and decide, quite reasonably, that it's hot.
summaries.MarcusW054: Two seasons in the founding era, 3–22 overall, and the author of the most enduring record in league history: 913 points in 2010, the lowest-scoring season anyone has ever managed. Sixteen years later it still stands, untouched and possibly untouchable. Immortality finds us in strange ways.
summaries.brodywhite1012: A founding-era owner who gave it two seasons and 7 wins, with a best finish of 9th in 2009. His lone highlight reel is a win over MarcusW054 — which, historians note, was the fantasy equivalent of beating the practice squad. Gone by 2011, missed by few record books.
summaries.j5narlock: Two founding seasons, 11–15, and — credit where due — he left on a three-game win streak in 2010. Retiring hot is a move most owners never master. The league will never know if it was the start of a dynasty or the universe's mercy rule.
summaries.ndirish1818: One season, 2011, finished 12th of 12 at 2–11. But within the wreckage: an 87-point ambush of juicebox269 that nobody saw coming, least of all juicebox269. Last place with one legendary scalp — there are worse ways to spend a single year.
summaries.rodneywoodcock: A two-season founding member who peaked at 7th in 2009 and put a 97-point hurting on future two-time champion adrenth01 along the way. The 2010 encore went 4–9, and that was that. Brief, occasionally violent, gone too soon.
